Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 55, English)
The Fundamental Stage: The 40-Day Sadhna That Builds Your First "Gola" — Brahmacharya, Neem-T ulsi, and the Jai Siyaram Jaap Pr ocedur e

Structural note: this session is a solo, dir ect-addr ess training video — a step-by-step pr ocedural instruction with no live sangat back-and-forth, named participant questions, or cr owd interaction. Per the standing template, this is ther efor e a 2-part document (Knowledge Base + Q&A Pairs only); Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) is intentionally omitted for this session.

1. Purpose of this video. This session explains, step by step, how a practitioner achieves and completes the Fundamental Stage — the first major milestone on the path described in the Foundation Course's overall roadmap.

2. Assumed prior context. This teaching assumes the viewer has already watched the earlier Foundation Course videos and understood the roadmap — the full arc runs from the practitioner's very first "gola" (ener gy circle/marker) all the way to the point where their kundalini shakti fully exits the body and connects them directly to the supreme power .

3. Why the guides stay involved until full r elease. Per this teaching, Bhaiya and the Ashaeiynn team stay actively involved as guides only until the practitioner's kundalini shakti has fully left the body; after that point, the practitioner is directly connected to the supreme power itself, which becomes a better guide than any human teacher .

4. Who can actually benefit fr om this sadhna. Only a person who has personally pur chased this Foundation Course as a legitimate member can progress through this sadhna — the shaktis involved are described as simply not activating for anyone else.

5. Watching or copying without membership does not work. If someone watches a member's practice and tries to replicate the procedure themselves without being a legitimate member , there is no harm in watching, but per this teaching the shaktis will not function for them — the practice will have no real ef fect.

6. What to do if you ar e not yet a legitimate member . Per this teaching, anyone unsure of their membership status, or not yet enrolled, should contact Bhaiya/Ashaeiynn directly before attempting this sadhna.
7. The first step for legitimate members: daily jaap. Once confirmed as a legitimate member , the practitioner's first concrete step is to begin a daily jaap practice.
8. Which mantra to use. Members connected to Ashaeiynn are given a specific mantra; per this teaching, anyone who performs jaap of this mantra begins to receive its benefit.
9. Overall duration of the Fundamental Stage pr ocess. The Fundamental Stage is described as an approximately 40-day pr ocess.
10. The requirement of brahmacharya during these 40 days. Throughout the 40 days, the practitioner must observe brahmacharya .

1 1. Reframing what "brahmacharya" actually means. Per this teaching, brahmacharya is deliberately not treated as an extreme, isolating lifestyle (avoiding "every single thing," as some interpret it); instead it is explained through the phrase "bhram ka
aacharan" — conduct free of illusion — meaning simply that the mind should be pure, and the person should clearly know their own true needs versus their desires.

12. Distinguishing "need" fr om "desir e." A practitioner should know the dif ference between a genuine need (necessity , which can be fulfilled without issue) and a desire (particularly one that arises unnecessarily in the mind) — per this teaching, it is desire, not legitimate need, that breaks brahmacharya.

13. Which desires to specifically avoid. Practitioners are advised, where possible, to avoid lustful desires or any desire that would pull them in a wrong direction — per this teaching, a person inherently knows for themselves what is right and wrong for them, more reliably than any third party telling them so.
14. Diet during the 40 days. Food should be kept light ("halka-phulka") — avoiding heavy or highly spicy food.
15. The morning neem-and-tulsi practice. Every morning, on an empty stomach, the practitioner should consume four neem leaves and four tulsi leaves .
16. How to take the neem leaves. Neem leaves may be consumed in any manner/method the practitioner prefers.

17. Why tulsi leaves must not be chewed. Tulsi leaves must specifically not be chewed — per this teaching, scripture (V ed-Puranas) explains this by saying tulsi is treated as Mata Tulsi and should be taken directly/reverently rather than chewed; Bhaiya adds a scientific rationale beneath this: tulsi leaves contain acid, while human teeth are chemically base, so chewing causes an acid-base neutralization reaction that weakens the teeth over time.
18. How to take tulsi pr operly . Tulsi should be taken the way one takes medicine directly with water , rather than chewed like ordinary food.

19. Leaves do not need to be fr esh daily . Per this teaching, it is not necessary to pluck fresh neem and tulsi leaves each day — they may be gathered in advance and stored (including refrigerated) for later use.

20. The cor e mantra for this sadhna: "Jai Siyaram." The specific jaap to be performed throughout this 40-day process is of "Jai Siyaram" — described as a Vijay Mantra (victory mantra) and a Mahamantra (great mantra).
21. Jaap should not be done while walking. For the full 40 days, this jaap should not be performed while walking around or moving through daily activity — it requires a dedicated, seated session.

22. Choosing when to sit for practice. The practitioner may choose any time they are free — there is no fixed requirement that it be morning or evening specifically — whenever they feel the pull to meditate and do what is needed.
23. Lighting the diya (lamp). At the chosen time, the practitioner should light a diya — using either ghee or oil, according to personal preference/availability .
24. Pr eparing a seat. Where possible, an asan (seat/mat) should be laid out and the practitioner should sit on it.
25. The diya must stay lit thr oughout the session. The lit diya should continue burning for the entire duration that the practitioner sits — from start to finish of the sitting.

26. Dedicating the diya to Hanuman Ji Maharaj. After lighting the diya, the practitioner takes water in hand and of fers a specific dedication prayer , naming Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj as the one to whom the diya is of fered.

27. The exact wording of the diya-dedication prayer . Per this teaching, the practitioner says: "I take Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya as witness and offer this diya at the sacr ed feet of Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj. O Ram-devotee Hanuman, O Hanuman Ji Maharaj, kindly accept this diya. My prayer is that you grant me devotion and power , and fully pr otect and safeguar d me." After this, the water held in hand is released onto the ground.

28. Reciting one's own ishta's stuti/aarti/chalisa. After the diya dedication, while still seated, the practitioner should — where possible — recite a stuti, aarti, or chalisa of their own personal ishta devta (chosen deity); it need not be Hanuman Ji specifically .

29. Dedicating the jaap itself, befor e starting. Before beginning the actual jaap, the practitioner again takes water in hand and of fers a second, separate dedication — this time for the jaap itself.

30. The exact wording of the jaap-dedication prayer . Per this teaching, the practitioner says: "I take Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya as witness and offer this jaap of mine at the sacr ed feet of Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj. O Ram-devotee Hanuman, kindly accept and r eceive this jaap." The water is then released onto the ground, and the jaap begins.
31. Minimum jaap duration and mala count. The practitioner should perform jaap for a minimum of 25 to 30 minutes , or , if counting via mala, complete 51 malas of "Jai Siyaram."
32. Volume of r ecitation. The jaap should be spoken aloud, loud enough that the practitioner's own ears can hear it — not silent, not merely mental repetition.

33. Weekly pr ogr ession and check-ins with Ashaeiynn. The first week's tar get is 25 minutes; after completing the first week, the practitioner should contact Bhaiya/Ashaeiynn so that progress can be guided based on the practitioner's individual grahan shakti (receptive capacity) — specifically how well the mantra is "settling" in their body — and the required jaap amount from then on is adjusted accordingly .

34. Gradual incr ease over the 40 days. Per this teaching, the jaap duration/time typically increases gradually week over week, reaching approximately two and a half hours by around the 40-day mark for most practitioners.
35. The closing hawan. Once the 40 days are complete, a hawan is performed for the practitioner .

36. Purpose of the closing hawan. The hawan serves the practitioner's ongoing raksha-suraksha (protection) and lets their devotion/power continue developing according to their individual receptive capacity; per this teaching, it is specifically structured to bring all 12 golas (ener gy circles/markers) to completion and fully "lock" the practitioner's body within their aura.

37. Why some pr ogr ess faster than others. Per this teaching, some practitioners naturally complete ("cover") this process faster than others — the closing hawan is designed to bring everyone's 12 golas to full completion regardless of individual pace.

38. Cr ossing into the next stage r equires this full lock. Only once the aura is completely , fully locked can a practitioner move on and cross out of the Fundamental Stage into the next stage of the path.

39. Physical and experiential effects during the 40 days. Practitioners may experience darshans (visions) during this period; while sitting and doing jaap, vibrations may be felt in the body — sensations such as heaviness in the head, or sudden coldness, are described as normal.

40. Encouragement to fully feel these sensations. Per this teaching, practitioners are encouraged to try to fully feel these sensations, continuing the "Jai Siyaram" jaap wholeheartedly — with mind, devotion, and body all engaged.

41. Reassurance about disturbed sleep and vivid dr eams. Around 10-12 days in, as bodily ener gy begins building, restlessness may increase — reduced sleep and more frequent dreams (in any direction/theme) are described as a normal and expected part of the process, since the body's "container" cannot yet fully hold the growing ener gy .

42. Reassurance about night-fall in male practitioners. Per this teaching, some male practitioners may experience night-fall (nocturnal emission) during this period; this is described as an expected consequence of the lower ener gy pathway having been opened, and practitioners are told not to worry about it.

43. Outward appearance vs. inward experience. Per this teaching, an observer might mistakenly interpret a practitioner's tiredness during this period as weakness, when in fact the practitioner's own body retains and knows its actual growing ener gy level.

44. Why weekly contact with Ashaeiynn matters. Practitioners are asked to stay in weekly contact so that Ashaeiynn can check their aura regularly and ensure this 40-day process completes properly and fully .

45. Why structur ed guidance shortens the timeline. Per this teaching, attempting this process entirely without guidance/support would typically take at least 3 to 4 months ; compressing that same process into 40 days requires stricter standards and precision, which is exactly why Ashaeiynn's structured guidance and the closing hawan matter .

46. A key r eassurance: the mantra does not override devotion to one's own ishta. Per this teaching, performing the "Jai Siyaram" jaap and dedicating it to Hanuman Ji Maharaj does not mean the practitioner's own personal ishta devta's shakti is bypassed — whichever deity the practitioner personally loves and is devoted to, it is that deity's shakti which the practitioner receives; this is described as a guaranteed promise ("vachan"), not a general claim.

47. Exception when Hanuman Ji is alr eady one's ishta. Per this teaching, if Hanuman Ji Maharaj already is the practitioner's own ishta devta, then of course it is his shakti specifically that is received — described as a matter of great good fortune in that case.

48. This is not disr espect toward other deities or mantras. Per this teaching, practicing this specific jaap and procedure should never be understood as criticizing, dismissing, or disrespecting any other deity or any other mantra tradition.

49. Effects for those who alr eady carry prior spiritual capacities. Per this teaching, some individuals already carry some prior drishti (subtle vision) or previously-acquired powers before starting; for such people, existing drishti may "dissolve"/refine further , and previously dormant powers may become newly awakened, during this same process.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

The Fundamental Stage is an approximately 40-day structured sadhna process, open only to legitimate, paying Foundation Course members — the shaktis involved will not work for non-members, even if they copy the procedure exactly . Brahmacharya during these 40 days is defined as "bhram ka aacharan" (illusion-free conduct/purity of mind) — knowing and honoring genuine needs while avoiding unnecessary or lustful desires — not an extreme ascetic lifestyle. Daily requirements: light food; four neem leaves and four tulsi leaves on an empty stomach each morning (tulsi must be swallowed with water like medicine, never chewed, for both scriptural and dental-chemistry reasons); leaves may be stored in advance. The core mantra is "Jai Siyaram" (a Vijay Mantra/Mahamantra), performed seated (never while walking), for a minimum of 2530 minutes or 51 malas daily , spoken loud enough to hear oneself, with duration increasing weekly toward roughly 2.5 hours by day 40. Each sitting requires: a lit diya (kept burning the whole session), an asan if possible, a specific water -in-hand dedication prayer of fering the diya to Hanuman Ji Maharaj (naming Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya as witness), optional recitation of one's own ishta's stuti/aarti/chalisa, then a second water -in-hand dedication prayer specifically of fering the jaap itself before beginning. Weekly check-ins with Ashaeiynn are required so the mantra count/duration can be adjusted to the practitioner's individual grahan shakti (receptive capacity), and so the practitioner's aura can be monitored throughout. The process closes with a hawan designed to complete all 12 golas and fully "lock" the practitioner's aura — only after this full lock can a practitioner cross into the next stage. Expected side ef fects (vibrations, head heaviness, coldness, reduced sleep, vivid dreams, night-fall in men) are normal signs of building ener gy , not weakness, and are not cause for worry . Without structured guidance, this same process would typically take 3-4 months rather than 40 days. Performing this jaap and dedicating it to Hanuman Ji Maharaj does not override or replace the practitioner's bond with their own personal ishta devta — the practitioner receives their own ishta's shakti specifically (Hanuman Ji's own shakti only if he is already that person's ishta) — and this practice is never to be understood as disrespect toward any other deity or mantra tradition.

The Fundamental Stage: The 40-Day Sadhna That Builds Your First "Gola" — Brahmacharya, Neem-T ulsi, and the Jai Siyaram Jaap Pr ocedur e

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn training session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siyaram." Note: this session is a solo training video with no live sangat interaction, so ther e is no Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) for this session — only Parts I and II.

Q1. What does this session actually teach? A: Step-by-step, how a practitioner achieves and completes the Fundamental Stage — the first major milestone described in the Foundation Course roadmap, running from a practitioner's very first "gola" to full kundalini release.

Q2. Who can actually benefit fr om following this 40-day sadhna? A: Per this teaching, only someone who has personally purchased the Foundation Course as a legitimate member — the shaktis involved simply do not activate for anyone else.

Q3. If I just watch a member practicing and copy the pr ocedur e myself, will it work for me? A: No — per this teaching, there's no harm in watching, but the shaktis will not function for a non-member , so the practice will have no real ef fect for them.
Q4. What should I do if I'm not sur e whether I'm a legitimate, enr olled member? A: Contact Bhaiya/Ashaeiynn directly before attempting this sadhna.
Q5. What is the very first concr ete step once someone is confirmed as a legitimate member? A: To begin a daily jaap practice of the specific mantra given to Ashaeiynn members.
Q6. Roughly how long does the Fundamental Stage pr ocess take? A: Approximately 40 days.

Q7. Does this teaching r equire strict, ascetic brahmacharya — avoiding all worldly engagement? A: No — per this teaching, brahmacharya is explained as "bhram ka aacharan" (illusion-free conduct), meaning a pure mind and clarity about one's genuine needs versus desires, not an extreme isolating lifestyle.

Q8. How does this teaching distinguish a "need" fr om a "desir e"? A: A need/necessity can be fulfilled without any issue; a desire — especially one arising unnecessarily in the mind — is what actually breaks brahmacharya if indulged.

Q9. Which kinds of desir es should a practitioner specifically try to avoid during these 40 days? A: Lustful desires or any desire pulling the practitioner in a wrong direction — per this teaching, a person inherently knows what is right or wrong for themselves better than any third party telling them.
Q10. What kind of diet should be followed during this period? A: Light food ("halka-phulka"), avoiding heavy or highly spicy meals.

Q1 1. What is the daily morning leaf practice, and how should it be done? A: Four neem leaves and four tulsi leaves, taken on an empty stomach each morning; neem may be consumed any way , but tulsi must never be chewed.

Q12. Why must tulsi leaves never be chewed? A: Scripturally , tulsi is treated as Mata Tulsi and taken directly/reverently rather than chewed; scientifically , per this teaching, tulsi contains acid while human teeth are chemically base, so chewing causes a neutralizing reaction that weakens teeth over time — tulsi should instead be taken like medicine, with water .
Q13. Do the neem and tulsi leaves need to be fr eshly picked each day? A: No — per this teaching, they can be gathered in advance and stored, including refrigerated, for later use.
Q14. What is the specific mantra used thr oughout this 40-day sadhna? A: "Jai Siyaram" — described as a Vijay Mantra (victory mantra) and Mahamantra (great mantra).

Q15. Can this jaap be done while walking ar ound during the day? A: No — per this teaching, for the full 40 days it must be done seated in a dedicated session, never while walking or moving through daily activity .

Q16. Is ther e a fixed time of day (morning or evening) r equired for this practice? A: No — per this teaching, the practitioner may sit at any time they are free, whenever they feel the pull to meditate and do what's needed.
Q17. What must be pr epar ed befor e starting a jaap session? A: A lit diya (using ghee or oil, per preference), and an asan/seat where possible — the diya must stay burning for the entire session.

Q18. What is the first prayer performed at the start of a session, and to whom is it addr essed? A: A dedication of the lit diya to Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj, spoken while holding water in hand, naming Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya as witness, asking Hanuman Ji to accept the diya and grant devotion, power , and full protection — after which the water is released onto the ground.

Q19. What should a practitioner do after the diya-dedication prayer , befor e starting the jaap itself? A: Where possible, recite the stuti, aarti, or chalisa of their own personal ishta devta (whichever deity they are personally devoted to).

Q20. Is ther e a second prayer befor e the jaap begins, and what is it for? A: Yes — again holding water in hand, the practitioner dedicates the jaap itself to Hanuman Ji Maharaj, naming Ashaeiynn's Parikshit Bhaiya as witness and asking him to accept and receive the jaap, then releasing the water before beginning.
Q21. How long should each day's jaap session last, at minimum? A: A minimum of 25 to 30 minutes, or 51 malas if counting by mala.
Q22. Should the jaap be done silently/mentally , or spoken aloud? A: Spoken aloud, loud enough that the practitioner's own ears can hear it.

Q23. What should a practitioner do after completing their first week of practice? A: Contact Bhaiya/Ashaeiynn so progress can be reviewed and the required jaap duration adjusted according to the practitioner's individual grahan shakti (receptive capacity).

Q24. Does the jaap duration stay fixed at 25 minutes for all 40 days? A: No — per this teaching, it typically increases gradually week by week, reaching roughly two and a half hours by around day 40 for most practitioners.

Q25. What happens once the 40 days ar e complete? A: A hawan is performed for the practitioner , designed to bring all 12 golas to full completion and completely "lock" the practitioner's body within their aura.

Q26. Why does this stage r equire the aura to be fully "locked" befor e moving on? A: Per this teaching, only once the aura is completely locked can a practitioner cross out of the Fundamental Stage into the next stage of the path.

Q27. Is it normal to feel physical sensations like heaviness in the head, coldness, or vibrations during this pr ocess? A: Yes — per this teaching, these are described as normal experiential ef fects, and practitioners are encouraged to try to fully feel them while continuing the jaap wholeheartedly .

Q28. Why might sleep get disturbed and dr eams incr ease ar ound 10-12 days into the pr ocess? A: Per this teaching, as bodily ener gy begins building, the body's "container" cannot yet fully hold the growing ener gy , causing increased restlessness, reduced sleep, and more frequent dreams — described as normal and expected.

Q29. Is night-fall (nocturnal emission) in male practitioners during this period something to worry about? A: No — per this teaching, it is described as an expected consequence of the lower ener gy pathway having opened, and practitioners are told not to be concerned about it.

Q30. Does performing this specific jaap and dedicating it to Hanuman Ji Maharaj mean I stop r eceiving my own personal ishta devta's blessings? A: No — per this teaching, this is a guaranteed promise: whichever deity the practitioner personally loves and is devoted to, it is that deity's own shakti which the practitioner receives (Hanuman Ji's own shakti specifically only applies if he is already that practitioner's ishta) — and this practice is never meant to disrespect any other deity or mantra tradition.

Keep the tulsi non-chewing rule and its dual justification (scriptural reverence + acid-base dental chemistry) both intact and clearly distinguished as two separate reasons given in this teaching. Encourage weekly check-ins with Ashaeiynn as a stated requirement of this teaching, not merely an optional suggestion.
